cohort: Pregnant Sprague Dawley rats orally administered BPA or control from pregnancy day 1 until gestation day 21, and their male offspring.
finding: Prenatal BPA exposure at 5 mg/kg/day significantly reduced the expression of miR-19a, miR-539, GRIN2A, and GRIN2B genes, and GluN2A and GluN2B protein levels in the male rat hippocampus, leading to spatial and fear memory impairments by adolescent age 35.
